questions.text: What is BUSY_CYCLES: does the tail push add a cycle (give the BUSY_CYCLES value)? (Scenario: After INIT, a message of 2 full words is pushed via PUSH4, followed by PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN 3 (5+... 11 bytes total).) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Yes, the tail push adds a cycle. BUSY_CYCLES counts one per clock in which a push is processed, and a PUSH_N with N>0 counts. The 2 PUSH4 words give 2 and the PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN 3 adds 1, so BUSY_CYCLES = 3 (BYTE_COUNT = 11).
questions.evidence: - BYTE_COUNT is 32 bits and wraps. BUSY_CYCLES counts one per clock in which a push is processed (PUSH4 or PUSH_N with N>0), it is 32 bits and wraps; a PUSH_N with N = 0 does not count.

questions.text: Does the ID register still read 0x20930001 after the write? (Scenario: CTRL bit 0 was written to 1 and then INIT is issued. A write to ID at 0x000 with 0xFFFFFFFF is also performed.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Yes. ID is read-only, so the write of 0xFFFFFFFF to 0x000 is ignored. INIT only clears the CRC state, BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES, so ID keeps reading 0x20930001.
questions.evidence: Writes to read-only registers are ignored.

questions.text: What does BUSY_CYCLES read after the wrapping push? (Scenario: BYTE_COUNT is 0xFFFFFFFC and one PUSH4 is issued making BYTE_COUNT wrap to 0. BUSY_CYCLES was 5 before the push.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
